or_philosopher_s_stone_the.blurb: A small sport wall in the Marsupials, the quiet far side of Smith Rock State Park above the Crooked River. It holds a dozen bolted lines, all in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, split roughly between the two grades, so it suits strong leaders rather than anyone warming up. Climbers describe the stone as red, clean and among the better rock in the park. The wall only catches the sun from mid-afternoon onward, which makes it a reasonable pick on hot days, but it sits in a wind funnel and can be too gusty to climb. Getting here takes a long hike across scree, so expect solitude.

or_swine_aka_enola_hill_the.blurb: A cliff on Enola Hill in the Mt. Hood National Forest, looking down on the town of Rhododendron. It sees few visitors. Of the twelve climbs recorded, eight are bolted sport lines and four are trad, running from easy 5.7 and 5.8 up to a cluster of 5.12s, with a handful of 5.10s in the middle. Routes are around 85 feet, with a mix of sidepulls, jugs and small roofs, and some loose rock low down on at least one line. A trail drops from the rim past a first wall to the main cliff. Good for strong climbers wanting a quiet day.
